hints: Sketch y=cot2x with asymptotes at 0 and π/2 and zero at π/4.
Sketch y=2sin2x−1 on the same radian axes and show exactly one intersection.
walkthrough:
Consider the two functions $y = \cot(2x)$ and $y = 2\sin(2x) - 1$ on the interval $0 < x < \dfrac{1}{2}\pi$:
$$\text{For } 0 < x < \dfrac{1}{2}\pi, \quad 0 < 2x < \pi$$

Analyze the behavior of each curve across this interval:
$$\text{The graph of } y = \cot(2x) \text{ decreases continuously from } +\infty \text{ as } 2x \to 0^+ \text{ to } -\infty \text{ as } 2x \to \pi^-,$$
$$\text{crossing the } x\text{-axis at } 2x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \implies x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}.$$

Analyze the sinusoidal curve $y = 2\sin(2x) - 1$:
$$\text{At } x = 0: \quad y = 2\sin(0) - 1 = -1$$
$$\text{At } x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}: \quad y = 2\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - 1 = 2(1) - 1 = 1$$
$$\text{At } x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}: \quad y = 2\sin(\pi) - 1 = 2(0) - 1 = -1$$

Conclude regarding the number of intersection points:
$$\text{Since } y = \cot(2x) \text{ decreases strictly from } +\infty \text{ to } -\infty \text{ while } y = 2\sin(2x) - 1 \text{ remains bounded in } [-1, 1],$$
$$\text{the two graphs intersect at exactly one point in the interval } 0 < x < \dfrac{1}{2}\pi.$$

hints: Evaluate f(0.4) and f(0.6), display opposite signs, and use continuity to justify the bracket.
walkthrough:
Define the difference function $f(x) = \cot(2x) - (2\sin(2x) - 1)$ for radians $x$:
$$f(x) = \dfrac{1}{\tan(2x)} - 2\sin(2x) + 1$$

Conclude using the intermediate value theorem:
$$\text{Since } f(0.4) > 0 \text{ and } f(0.6) < 0, \text{ and } f(x) \text{ is continuous on } [0.4, 0.6],$$
$$\text{a root of the equation lies in the interval } 0.4 < x < 0.6.$$

hints: Use the stated inverse-tangent update in radians, starting with x₁=0.5000.
Record every iterate to 4 decimal places until the alternating values justify a 2-decimal-place root.
walkthrough:
Apply the iterative formula $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sin(2x_n) - 1}\right)$ starting with $x_1 = 0.5000$ (in radian mode):
$$2x_1 = 1.0000 \implies \sin(1.0000) \approx 0.841471$$
$$2\sin(1.0000) - 1 = 1.682942 - 1 = 0.682942$$
$$x_2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{0.682942}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(1.464253) \approx \dfrac{1}{2}(0.971618) \approx 0.4858$$

Compute successive iterations to 4 decimal places:
$$x_3 = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sin(2 \times 0.4858) - 1}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sin(0.9716) - 1}\right) \approx 0.4967$$
$$x_4 = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sin(2 \times 0.4967) - 1}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sin(0.9934) - 1}\right) \approx 0.4883$$
$$x_5 = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sin(2 \times 0.4883) - 1}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sin(0.9766) - 1}\right) \approx 0.4947$$
$$x_6 \approx 0.4899, \quad x_7 \approx 0.4934, \quad x_8 \approx 0.4907, \quad x_9 \approx 0.4928$$

Conclude the value of the root correct to 2 decimal places:
$$\text{All iterates oscillating around } 0.491 \text{ round to } 0.49:$$
$$x = 0.49$$
